edition.window: Orders and decisions passed or reported between 10:00 AM IST on 15 October 2026 and 11:00 AM IST on 16 October 2026

items.caseName: Girraj Bansal v. Rakesh Kumar Goyal
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member) and Indevar Pandey (Technical Member)
items.headline: TDS and GST credit prove supply; CIRP upheld
items.text: The NCLAT upheld the admission of Shri Paramsukh Edible Foods into CIRP on a mustard-seed supplier's claim of about Rs 1.42 crore in principal. It treated the debtor's own TDS deductions, input tax credit claims on the supplier's invoices and ledger entries as proof that the goods were supplied and received. A PIN code discrepancy in the invoices did not show non-supply, particularly since the debtor never raised a query about non-receipt.

items.caseName: Sanjit Instruments Private Limited & Ors v. Arvind Jagannath Bagul
items.coram: Justice Sharad Kumar Sharma (Judicial Member), Arun Baroka and Indevar Pandey (Technical Members)
items.headline: No share buyout without oppression finding
items.text: The Appellate Tribunal ruled that the NCLT cannot direct a buyout under Section 242(2)(b) of the Companies Act unless it first records a finding of oppression and mismanagement under Section 241 and the satisfaction needed under Section 242(1). It set aside an NCLT Mumbai buyout order that relied on a 2018 valuation, holding that any valuation must be close in time to the decision. The case goes back to NCLT Mumbai for a fresh valuation and a decision on the merits.

items.caseName: Shruti Lohia, Resolution Professional for Arihant Retail Private Limited
items.coram: Sanjiv Jain (Judicial Member) and Venkataraman Subramaniam (Technical Member)
items.headline: Pothys Retail's Rs 43 crore plan for Arihant cleared
items.text: The Chennai Bench approved Pothys Retail's resolution plan for Arihant Retail, which the committee of creditors had backed unanimously. It found the plan met Sections 30 and 31 of the IBC and the CIRP Regulations. The plan is valued at Rs 43.02 crore and includes a proposed Rs 15 crore infusion. The Bench granted some of the reliefs sought and left certain tax and statutory reliefs to the authorities concerned.

items.caseName: In re Composite Scheme of Arrangement between HSBC InvestDirect Sales & Marketing (India) Pvt. Ltd. and HSBC InvestDirect (India) Pvt. Ltd.
items.coram: K.R. Saji Kumar (Judicial Member) and Anil Raj Chellan (Technical Member)
items.headline: First motion cleared for HSBC InvestDirect merger
items.text: The Mumbai Bench allowed the first motion for merging two HSBC InvestDirect companies, together with a reduction of the transferor's share capital. The 1% stake held by an employee welfare trust will be cancelled for Rs 283.90 a share. Shareholder meetings were dispensed with on the basis of consent affidavits, and creditor meetings were waived because there are no secured creditors and unsecured creditors are protected by undertakings.

items.caseName: Director General of Anti-Profiteering v. Mangalbela Real Estates Pvt. Ltd.
items.headline: Builder must pass Rs 31.2 lakh ITC benefit to buyers
items.text: The tribunal found that the developer of the Atri Green Valley project in Kolkata breached Section 171(1) of the CGST Act by keeping the additional input tax credit benefit instead of passing it to homebuyers. It rejected objections to the re-investigation and held that the time limit for the investigation report is directory. The company must pay about Rs 31.2 lakh to 66 homebuyers within three months with 18% interest. No penalty was imposed because the period of profiteering ended before Section 171(3A) came into force.

items.headline: Price escalation: interest runs on extra GST
items.text: In a matter in which Mukand Limited was the respondent, the Bengaluru Bench held that when prices go up after supply under escalation clauses, interest on the extra GST runs from the original due date. This applies even if the additional tax is paid later through debit notes or supplementary invoices. The goods in question were cleared between April and June 2017.

items.headline: 180-day ITC lapse alone no ground for s.74 penalty
items.text: The Thiruvananthapuram Bench held that failing to reverse input tax credit after not paying suppliers within 180 days does not, on its own, justify a penalty under Section 74 of the CGST Act. A penalty under that section needs a specific, supportable allegation of suppression or the other elements the provision requires. The dispute arose from an audit of a jewellery firm covering January 2019 to March 2021.

items.caseName: A.P. Constructions India Pvt. Ltd. v. Commissioner of GST & Central Excise
items.caseNo: Service Tax Appeal Nos. 41344 of 2016, 40299 of 2022 and 40300 of 2022
items.coram: P. Dinesha (Judicial Member) and M. Ajit Kumar (Technical Member)
items.headline: Builder's service tax demands remanded
items.text: CESTAT Chennai set aside service tax orders against a builder and its managing director and ordered fresh adjudication within 90 days. It held that flats allotted to landowners cannot be taxed as construction consideration without proof, and that any such value must be fixed under Section 67 and the valuation rules. The adjudicating authority must also re-examine classification, the GTA, security and manpower components, limitation and penalties.

items.caseName: Bharat Aluminium Company Limited v. Commissioner of Central Excise & CGST (Audit), Indore
items.coram: Rachna Gupta (Officiating President) and P.V. Subba Rao (Technical Member)
items.headline: BALCO water deal is a sale, not a taxable service
items.text: The tribunal held that BALCO's agreement with Chhattisgarh's Water Resources Department was a sale of water, not an assignment of a right to use natural resources. It set aside a service tax demand of Rs 7.29 crore on the merits and on limitation. It also found the issue revenue-neutral, because any tax paid under reverse charge could have been taken as CENVAT credit.

items.caseName: Regional Manager, Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation v. Commissioner, CGST & Central Excise, Allahabad
items.coram: P.K. Choudhary (Judicial Member) and K. Anpazhakan (Technical Member)
items.headline: UPSRTC's Yatri Plaza dhaba fees not taxable
items.text: CESTAT Allahabad set aside a Rs 3.85 lakh demand on amounts UPSRTC collected from roadside dhabas under its Yatri Plaza Yojna. It found no quid pro quo with the dhaba owners and treated the scheme as a welfare measure for passengers. The arrangement was held not to be a declared service, business auxiliary service or renting of property. Stops at designated dhabas were treated as part of the passenger transport service.

items.caseName: Rajasthan State Road Development & Construction Corporation Limited v. Commissioner of CGST, Customs and Central Excise, Jodhpur-I
items.coram: Ajay Sharma (Judicial Member) and Hemambika R. Priya (Technical Member)
items.headline: Sale of tender documents is not a service
items.text: The tribunal held that fees for selling tender documents do not attract service tax when only the prescribed cost of the documents is collected, because no identifiable service passes from the tendering authority to the bidder. It set aside the demand, interest and penalty, following its earlier ruling in Rajcomp Info Services.

items.caseName: Cliantha Research Ltd v. Commissioner of Central Excise and Service Tax
items.coram: Somesh Arora (Judicial Member) and Sanjiv Srivastava (Technical Member)
items.headline: Corporate guarantee for group firm not taxable
items.text: The appellant had arranged a bank guarantee for a foreign sister concern. CESTAT Ahmedabad held that giving such a corporate guarantee is neither a banking and financial service nor an intermediary service, because the parties dealt on a principal-to-principal basis. The service tax demands were set aside and the appeal was allowed.

items.headline: CCI clears GRT Jewellers' majority stake in TBZ
items.text: The Competition Commission approved GRT Jewellers (India) Pvt. Ltd.'s proposed acquisition of a majority shareholding in the listed jeweller Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri Ltd. The Commission said a detailed order will follow.
